texts.preamble: Kartik Chand Sharma vs Mubarik Ali. on 19 August, 2023 In The Court Of Ms. Mayuri Singh Presiding Officer : Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, East District : Karkardooma Courts Delhi Cnr No.: Dlet01-000484-2019 Macp No.95/19 Kartik Chand Sharma versus Mubarik Ali.
texts.facts: The present claim petition is based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed under section 159/166 clause (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (herein after Act) by the investigating officer of FIR No.75/18 Police Station Gandhi Nagar, Delhi. 2. Briefly narrated facts of the present case are that the accident in the present case took place on 20.03.2018. It is the case of the petitioner that on 20.03.2018 at around 9:35 PM, he was riding on his bicycle and when he reached at Pusta Road, Mother Dairy, Kailash Nagar Red Light, PS Gandhi Nagar, Delhi, offending truck bearing registration No. HR-74A-2929, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from the back side and without blowing any horn and applying safety measures, the driver of the offending vehicle hit the petitioner from back side, due to which he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries. Petitioner was admitted in SDN Hospital, Dilshad Kartik Chand Sharma vs Mubarik Ali. on 19 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116206995/ 1 Garden, Delhi wherein MLC was prepared. 3. On notice of the petition, the respondent no. 1 & 2 appeared with counsel at the time of filing of DAR. The respondents no. 1 and 2 who are the driver and owner of the offending truck filed written statement. Written Statement was also filed by R-3/insurance. In the written statement filed by R-1 and R-2, it is stated that no accident was caused by the vehicle bearing registration No. HR-74A-2929 and they have been falsely implicated in collusion with injured. Accident was caused because injured was not plying his bicyle properly and lost control. R-1 had valid DL and offending vehicle was duly insured. R-3 / insurer has mentioned in its written statement that the DAR is incomplete and the offending truck was dangerously loaded, as per para 66 of DAR, which is violation of permit condition but IO has not provided the photographs of the vehicle and particulars of the goods. The offending vehicle bears Hayana Registration number but IO has filed RC issued by RTO, Baghpat, U.P. The site-plan is incomplete and no independent eye witness was examined. There was contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner for riding his bicycle in the middle of the road. (iv) Relief 5. In order to establish his claim, petitioner Kartik Chand Sharma has examined himself as PW-1 and exhibited in evidence his medical treatment record and bills, pan card and aadhar card and DAR. Dr. Sanjeev Gambhir was examined as PW-2 and proved on recorded the disability certificate Ex.PW-2/A and assessment sheet Ex.PW-2/B. The respondents have not led any evidence.

In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima-facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act. If any party does not accept such a charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence. In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable. 16. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases. It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured , comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. on 19 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116206995/ 7 SC 752 and Sohan Lal vs. Taj Khan & Ors., 2019 ACJ 252, Rajasthan High Court).
